_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 33 (Esau reunion; Jacob settles at Shechem). Saadia-specific: v.10 'כרויא וג'ה אלאשארף' = 'like the seeing of the face of nobility' (Saadia takes 'as one sees the face of God' as 'as one sees the face of a noble/dignitary' — anti-anthropomorphic); v.14 'אלשראה' = al-Sharah (Esau's region, consistent with B14:6, B32:4); v.17 סוכות=Sukkot (transliterated); v.18 'נאבלס' = Nablus for Shechem (consistent with B12:6); v.20 'אלטאיק אלאה אסראיל' = 'the Power, God of Israel' (anti-anthropomorphic).

translations.1: Then Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked — and behold, Esau was coming, and four hundred men with him. And he divided the children between Leah and Rachel and the two maidservants.
translations.2: And he set the maidservants and their children first, and Leah and her children after them, and Rachel and Joseph after that.
translations.3: And he went on ahead of them; and he bowed down upon the earth seven times, until he drew near to his brother.
translations.4: And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him; and he fell upon his neck and kissed him; and they wept.
translations.5: And he lifted up his eyes, and saw the women and the children, and said: 'Who are these with you?' And he said: 'The children whom God has granted your servant.'
translations.6: Then the maidservants drew near, with their children, and bowed down.
translations.7: And Leah too drew near, with her children, and bowed down; and after that, Joseph drew near, and Rachel, and they bowed down.
translations.8: And he said: 'What is the meaning of all this camp which I met?' He said: 'To find favor with my lord.'
translations.9: Esau said: 'I have abundance — more than that. Keep what is yours, my brother.'
translations.10: Jacob said: 'No, my lord — if I have found favor with you, accept my gift from my hand; for I have seen your face as one sees the face of a dignitary; and you have been pleased with me.
translations.11: Accept my gift which has been brought to you; for God has been gracious to me, and I have abundance.' And he urged him, until he accepted it.
translations.12: He said to him: 'Let us journey on and go; and I shall travel with you.'
translations.13: He said to him: 'My lord knows that the children are tender, and that the sheep and cattle are nursing with me; if they are driven hard one day, much of them shall die.
translations.14: Let my lord pass on ahead of his servant; and I shall lead them slowly, on account of the property which is with me and on account of the children, until I come to my lord at al-Sharah (Seir).'
translations.15: He said: 'Then let me leave with you some of the people who are with me.' He said: 'Why? — let me but find this favor with my lord.'
translations.16: And Esau returned that day on his way to al-Sharah.
translations.17: And Jacob journeyed to Sukkot; and he built himself a house, and made booths for his cattle; therefore he named that place Sukkot.
translations.18: And Jacob came in safety to the town of Nablus (Shechem), which is in the land of Canaan, on his coming from Paddan-Aram; and he encamped over against the town.
translations.19: And he bought the field which adjoined the property where he had pitched his tent, from the hand of the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, for a hundred ewes.
translations.20: Then he built an altar; and he called upon it by the name of the Power, the God of Israel.
